storage: local Docker named volume; loopback HTTP; no TLS or artificial network delay
limitations: Short probes identify candidate rates, not sustained or 30-day capacity.
Shared host workloads may affect results; no other containers are stopped.
SDK events and adapter wire output are recorded once, then replayed with new identities.
Verification retains encoded replay descriptions, releases them page by page and accumulates per-view summaries; every complete payload is reconstructed and checked after restart.
OTLP batching and gzip model a gateway; SDK adapters still send one event per request.
Request latency starts after serialization/compression; preparation and schedule lag are reported separately.
Resource sampling includes Docker exec overhead and may miss peaks. Container memory includes filesystem cache.
Scheduled retention scans run every five seconds with a 30-day TTL; these runs do not measure deletion of expired data.

Optional aggregate profiling covers the process lifetime, including preload, health checks and startup retention, but excludes schema initialization and final checkpoint. It is unavailable after SIGKILL. Queue depth and internal timing percentiles are not measured.
Image ID identifies the executable. Git source provenance is the local checkout and cannot attest to a separately supplied image.

measurement_notes: The wrapper stopped and restored 13 development containers. The generic runner limitation saying no other containers are stopped does not apply to this run.

The same image, collector source hashes, workload plan, container limits, safety guards and service thresholds were used as the earlier stability attempt. Only the generator launcher/heap budget and memory reporting changed.

The test stopped when sampled cgroup memory.current crossed 1800 MiB. This includes filesystem cache; the sample does not distinguish anonymous memory, file cache or reclaimability. It is not evidence of an OOM kill or a leak.

All aggregate ingestion and query p95 thresholds passed over the shortened run. The video-list p95 in the final partial minute exceeded 500 ms. Both overall pass flags remain false because the planned duration was not completed.
The generator omitted 702 due requests; 572186 planned requests were never reached before the safety stop. They are distinct counts.

The profile includes preload, health checks and startup retention. Queue drain_ms=70.48 is an aborted wait: memory safety ended polling while the last sample still had 4850 pending events. No empty-queue sample was recorded. Graceful shutdown subsequently completed persistence; shutdown_ms=2079.25 includes other shutdown work and is not an isolated drain duration.
Host memory samples cover preload, traffic, verification and restoration and cannot attribute pressure to a single process.
The runner gracefully restarted and verified every acknowledged payload, context, envelope, summary and pagination check before removing the disposable test volume.

evidence_review.corrected_finding: The 70.48 ms queue wait aborted on memory safety with 4850 pending events; persistence completed during graceful shutdown. Both the narrative and JSON notes were corrected and rechecked.
